title: Mimi, Gus, and the Starry Pond
markdown:
Mimi the mouse was teeny-tiny. Her whiskers wiggled when she was excited. Her laugh sounded like little bells going ting-a-ling. She loved to explore the sunny meadow, little feet going patter-patter-patter on the soft ground, sniffing out sweet clover and juicy wild strawberries. Gus the goose was big and friendly. His feathers were fluffy white clouds. His honk was a happy rumble that always made Mimi giggle. They shared secrets with the wind and happy dreams under the big blue sky.

One bright afternoon they were playing catch-the-flitter-fly near Mimi’s snug little home. A shadow zipped by, quick as a falling leaf, but much faster. It was Flicker the dragonfly. His wings shimmered like a rainbow. He did not buzz with his usual zip. He landed with a little wobble on Gus’s smooth beak. His wings drooped.

“Oh, Gus,” he whispered, voice shaky like a thin thread. “Mimi. I need your help. I’m trying to find a pond. A special pond where the stars look super bright. I’m so sleepy, and I just can’t remember where it is.”

Mimi’s whiskers twitched. “A pond with bright stars? That sounds like a wonderful place. Do they twinkle more there?”

Gus nodded his big feathery head. “A pond where the stars are brightest must be very special. But which pond do you mean? There are many pretty ponds in our woods, shining like fallen pieces of the sky.”

Flicker drooped even more. “That’s the tricky part. I just can’t quite remember. It’s like a wispy cloud, just out of my thoughts. Or a dream you forget when you wake up.”

“Don’t worry, Flicker,” chirped Mimi. She hopped onto Gus’s wide back and snuggled near his soft neck feathers. “We’ll help you find it. Won’t we, Gus?”

Gus puffed out his chest. “Of course. A good friend always helps another friend. We’ll find that pond, even if it’s as far as the moon. Let’s ask our friends. The forest is full of friends who know many things.”

Flicker felt a little braver. He perched on Gus’s head, tiny antennae pointing the way. They waddled and scurried toward the sounds of the woods. The air smelled sweet with pine needles and damp earth.

First they met Pipkin the squirrel, always busy burying nuts, bushy tail flicking this way and that. He stopped, a shiny brown nut in his paws.

“Pipkin, busy squirrel,” honked Gus, friendly and calm. “Have you seen a pond where the stars look extra bright? Flicker needs to find it.”

Pipkin twitched his nose. “A pond with bright stars? I haven’t seen that. But I did see a very sparkly path just past those tall feathery ferns. It danced in the sunlight. Maybe it goes somewhere special.”

“Thank you, Pipkin,” squeaked Mimi, waving a little paw. Pipkin went back to his important nut-burying. They set off toward the happy sound of trickling water. A little brook giggled as it tumbled over smooth pebbles. Friendly flutterbys danced around them, wings like painted silk. A giggling frog with big round eyes peeked from under a wide green lily pad.

“Ribbit. Hello there. Are you looking for something?”

“We’re looking for a special pond,” explained Mimi.

“Ribbit. Special ponds are my favourite. Follow this brook. It leads to a quiet, peaceful place. You can’t miss it.”

Gus looked all around. “Look. Pipkin was right. I see a sparkly path through the tall grass.”

They followed it. It felt like walking on soft moonlight, even though the sun was still shining. It tickled Mimi’s paws and made Flicker’s wings hum. Soon they arrived at a beautiful clear pond. The water was so still and blue it looked like a piece of the sky had landed on the earth. Dragonflies zipped over the top. Tiny fish swam underneath.

“Is this it, Flicker?” asked Mimi, bouncing a little.

Flicker looked around. His delicate wings fluttered. He took a deep breath and sighed a tiny sad sigh. “It’s lovely. So still and so blue. But it’s not the one. The stars don’t look brightest here.” He looked down at his tiny feet. A little bit of sadness settled around him like a soft grey blanket.

The sun was beginning to dip behind the tall trees. Shadows grew longer across the meadow. The path ahead might become a little dim.

“Oh dear,” whispered Mimi. Her whiskers drooped. She patted Flicker gently. “Don’t be sad. We’re still here with you. We can still look.”

Gus nudged Flicker softly with his beak. “Even if we don’t find your special pond tonight, we are together.”

Flicker felt a little better. A tiny spark of hope. But he still wished he could find his special place. He felt so very tired.

Then Gus’s eyes lit up. A memory popped into his head, what his wise old aunt goose used to say on clear nights.

“Wait. Flicker. Mimi. I remember. My aunt told me about a pond. She said it only shows its brightest stars when the moon is high and the water is perfectly still. It reflects the stars, like a mirror for the sky.”

“Reflects?” squeaked Mimi. Her ears perked up.

“Yes. Like a mirror. Come this way. I think I know where it is.”

Gus led them on a new path, quieter, winding between big old trees that seemed to whisper secrets. Soon they arrived at another pond, even more still than the last, as if it were holding its breath. They waited. As the big silvery moon climbed higher, stars, one by one, started to twinkle in the water. They looked like a million tiny diamonds on dark velvet, shining even brighter than the stars in the sky above.

“Oh,” gasped Flicker, tiny wings fluttering with joy. His tiredness melted away like frost in the morning sun. “It is. It’s the moonbeam pond. The stars look so bright, so beautiful.” He zipped and zoomed over the water. The star reflections danced and shimmered, making the pond look like a secret door to the starry sky.

Mimi and Gus watched. Their hearts felt warm and full. They looked at Flicker, so happy, then at each other, sharing a smile. A pond where the stars look brightest, found together.

They sat at the still water a little longer, Mimi’s whiskers quiet, Gus’s feathers ruffled by the night, Flicker’s wings humming like tiny bells, until the moon was high and the meadow was ready for sleep.
